title: The report? I've finished it
goal: At the office, tell Maryam what you have and haven't done, putting the topic first: il-mudīr, ma shiftah 'the manager, I haven't seen him'
tip: To stress what you're talking about, say it first and point back to it with an ending: il-mudīr, ma shiftah 'the manager, I haven't seen him'; it-taqrīr khallaṣtah 'the report, I've finished it'. For things in the plural the ending is -ha: il-argām gāʿid ashūfha.
grammar: topic first with a resumptive pronoun (il-mudīr, ma shiftah); -ha for things in the plural
dialogue: A
صباح الخير. المدير يسأل عنك من الصبح
ṣabāḥ il-khēr. il-mudīr yisʼal ʿannak min iṣ-ṣubḥ
Good morning. The manager's been asking for you since first thing.
B
صباح النور. المدير؟ والله ما شفته اليوم
ṣabāḥ in-nūr. il-mudīr? wallāh ma shiftah il-yōm
Good morning. The manager? Honestly, I haven't seen him today.
A
يبي التقرير. التقرير، خلصته ولّا بعد؟
yabi t-taqrīr. it-taqrīr, khallaṣtah walla baʿad?
He wants the report. The report: have you finished it, or not yet?
B
التقرير خلصته، بس الأرقام للحين قاعد أشوفها
it-taqrīr khallaṣtah, bas il-argām lil-ḥīn gāʿid ashūfha
The report, I've finished it, but the figures, I'm still going through them.
A
حلو. والملاحظات اللي طرشتها أمس على التعديلات، شفتها؟
ḥilu. w il-mulāḥaẓāt illi ṭarrasht-ha ams ʿala t-taʿdīlāt, shift-ha?
Good. And the comments on the changes that I sent yesterday, have you seen them?
B
هيه، الملاحظات شفتها، وبخلصها اليوم إن شاء الله
hē, il-mulāḥaẓāt shift-ha, w bakhalliṣha l-yōm in shāʼ allāh
Yes, the comments, I've seen them, and I'll get them done today, God willing.
A
زين. المدير، الأحسن تروح له انت قبل لا يتصل فيك
zēn. il-mudīr, il-aḥsan trūḥ-lah inta gabil la yittaṣil fīk
OK. The manager: you'd better go to him yourself before he rings you.
B
صح كلامج. المدير بروح له الحين
ṣaḥḥ kalāmich. il-mudīr barūḥ-lah il-ḥīn
You're right. The manager, I'll go to him now.
items: khallaṣtah walla baʿad? = have you finished it or not yet?
the report, I've finished it; I've finished the report
the topic comes first and -ah 'it' points back to it
I'm going through them, I'm looking at them (things) (said by a man)
a woman says: gāʿda ashūfha (قاعدة أشوفها); things in the plural take -ha: il-argām … ashūfha
the comments, the feedback (on a piece of work)
the changes, the edits (to a document)
I'll finish them, I'll get them done; I'll finish it (f.)
you go to him, you go and see him (to a man)
he rings you, he calls you (to a man)
to a woman: yittaṣil fīch (يتصل فيج)
task: This week: search YouTube for «سوالف» (chats) or «بودكاست إماراتي» (Emirati podcast). Listen for 5 minutes and write down two sentences that put the topic first, like il-mudīr, ma shiftah. Within a minute you should hear شو / مب (UAE) or شنو / مو (Kuwait). If you hear سوف, ليس or هل all the time, it's fuṣḥā: pick another clip.

title: Dinner you pay, the coffee's on me
goal: At a restaurant with Sēf, argue over who pays, putting the thing or the person you're stressing first
tip: Put first what you're contrasting: il-ʿasha idfaʿah inta, bas il-gahwa ʿalay 'dinner, you pay for it, but the coffee's on me'. A pronoun before the verb stresses the person: ana badfaʿah 'I'm paying for it'; ana ma ṭalabtah 'I didn't order it'; mub ana 'not me'.
grammar: fronting for emphasis and contrast (il-ʿasha idfaʿah inta; ana ma ṭalabtah)
dialogue: A
يلا، الحساب علي اليوم
yalla, il-ḥsāb ʿalay il-yōm
Come on, the bill's on me today.
B
لا والله! حساب اليوم أنا بدفعه
la wallāh! ḥsāb il-yōm ana badfaʿah
No way! Today's bill, I'm paying it.
A
بس انت دفعت المرة اللي طافت
bas inta difaʿt il-marra illi ṭāfat
But you paid last time.
B
لا، المرة اللي طافت فهد دفع، مب أنا
la, il-marra illi ṭāfat Fahad difaʿ, mub ana
No, last time Fahad paid, not me.
A
زين، العشا ادفعه انت، بس القهوة علي
zēn, il-ʿasha idfaʿah inta, bas il-gahwa ʿalay
Fine: dinner, you pay for it, but the coffee's on me.
B
اتفقنا. بس الكيك هذا، منو طلبه؟ أنا ما طلبته
ittafagna. bas il-kēk hādha, minu ṭalabah? ana ma ṭalabtah
Deal. But this cake, who ordered it? I didn't order it.
A
الكيك هذا المطعم يقدمه حق كل الزباين، وببلاش بعد
il-kēk hādha l-maṭʿam yigaddmah ḥagg kill iz-zbāyin, w b-balāsh baʿad
This cake, the restaurant gives it to all its customers, and for free too.
B
ما شاء الله! هالمطعم بنرجع له أكيد
mā shāʼ allāh! hal-maṭʿam binirjaʿ-lah akīd
Wow! This restaurant, we'll definitely come back to it.
items: I'm paying for it, I'll pay it (me, not you)
I didn't order it (m.); you didn't order it (to a man)
to a woman: ma ṭalabtīh (ما طلبتيه)

title: You said what?!
goal: On the phone, react to Sēf's news with the question word at the end: gilt shu? 'you said what?'
tip: Gulf speakers often leave the question word where the answer would go, at the end. It adds surprise or stress: gilt shu?! 'you said what?!', tgūl shu? 'you're saying what?', shift minu? 'you saw who?'. A calm question puts it first, as before: shu gilt?
grammar: question word at the end for surprise and stress (gilt shu?, shift minu?)
dialogue: A
ترا بعت سيارتي اليوم
tara biʿt sayyārti l-yōm
Just so you know, I sold my car today.
B
قلت شو؟! بعتها؟ ليش؟
gilt shu?! biʿtha? lēsh?
You said what?! You sold it? Why?
A
كانت قديمة، وكل شهر تخرب. وشريت وحدة يديدة، وكالة!
kānat gadīma, w kill shahar tikhrab. w shirēt waḥda yidīda, wakāla!
It was old, and every month it broke down. And I've bought a new one, brand new from the dealer!
B
تقول شو؟ شريت سيارة يديدة؟
tgūl shu? shirēt sayyāra yidīda?
You're saying what? You've bought a new car?
A
هيه، وفي المعرض شفت واحد تعرفه، وهو بعد شرى وحدة مثلها
hē, w fi l-maʿraẓ shift wāḥid taʿarfah, w huwa baʿad shara waḥda mithilha
Yes, and at the showroom I saw someone you know, and he bought one like it too.
B
شفت منو؟ قول!
shift minu? gūl!
You saw who? Tell me!
A
الدكتور حقكم في الجامعة! باكر بتشوف السيارتين عند الجامعة
id-diktōr ḥaggkum fi l-jāmʿa! bāchir bitshūf is-sayyārtēn ʿind il-jāmʿa
Your lecturer at the university! Tomorrow you'll see both cars at the university.
B
ما صدقت! زين، بس سيارتك لونها شو؟
ma ṣaddagt! zēn, bas sayyārtak lōnha shu?
I can't believe it! OK, but your car, what colour is it?
A
هذا سر! بتعرف بروحك
hādha sirr! bitaʿarf b-rūḥak
That's a secret! You'll find out for yourself.
items: to a woman: gilti shu? (قلتي شو؟); a calm question: shu gilt?
you're saying what? what did you say?! (to a man)
to a woman: tgūlīn shu? (تقولين شو؟)
to a woman: shifti minu? (شفتي منو؟)
you sold it (f.), to a man: biʿtha (بعتها)
I bought; you bought (to a man)
to a woman: shirēti (شريتي); ishtarēt (اشتريت) means the same
at the showroom; at the exhibition
brand new (a car, straight from the dealer)

title: The flats are all new
goal: Look at flat ads with Sēf and talk about rooms, parking and shops, with feminine singular agreement for things in the plural
tip: Plural things usually take the feminine singular: is-sayyārāt yidīda 'the cars are new', il-maḥallāt tsakkir badri 'the shops close early', il-ghuraf ṣghīra. For people use the plural: ish-shabāb zēnīn.
grammar: agreement with non-human plurals: feminine singular (il-maḥallāt tsakkir, il-ghuraf ṣghīra)
dialogue: A
شوف هالشقق! كلها يديدة وقريبة من المترو
shūf hash-shigag! killha yidīda w garība min il-mitrō
Look at these flats! They're all new and close to the metro.
B
حلوة، بس الأسعار؟ أكيد غالية
ḥilwa, bas il-asʿār? akīd ghālya
Nice, but the prices? They must be expensive.
A
لا، مب وايد غالية. بس الغرف صغيرة شوي
la, mub wāyid ghālya. bas il-ghuraf ṣghīra shwayy
No, they're not that expensive. But the rooms are a bit small.
B
الغرف الصغيرة ما تفرق معي. المهم المواقف
il-ghuraf iṣ-ṣghīra ma tfarrig maʿi. il-muhimm il-mawāgif
Small rooms make no difference to me. What matters is the parking.
A
المواقف تحت العمارة، وكلها مظللة، يعني الشمس ما توصل السيارات
il-mawāgif taḥt il-ʿimāra, w killha mẓallala, yaʿni sh-shams ma tōṣal is-sayyārāt
The parking's under the building, and it's all shaded, so the sun doesn't get to the cars.
B
زين. والمحلات؟ قريبة؟
zēn. w il-maḥallāt? garība?
Good. And the shops? Are they close?
A
المحلات كلها تحت، بس تسكر بدري شوي
il-maḥallāt killha taḥt, bas tsakkir badri shwayy
The shops are all downstairs, but they close a bit early.
B
يعني الشقق هذي زينة، بس مب لي. أنا أحب مردف!
yaʿni sh-shigag hādhi zēna, bas mub li. ana aḥibb Mirdif!
So these flats are good, but they're not for me. I love Mirdif!
items: il-ghuraf ṣghīra = the rooms are small
the sun doesn't get (to it), it's out of the sun

title: Checkpoint 4.3: news of the rent at the majlis
goal: Checkpoint: in Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Sēf there, answer his questions about your flat and the landlord, respectfully
tip: Review: topic first (ṣāḥib ish-shigga, ma shifnāh), the question word at the end (simaʿt shu?), -ha and feminine agreement for things (il-umūr hādhi), a guess with atwaggaʿ, and respectful replies to an elder: yā ʿammi, ʿala ʿēni w rāsi.
grammar: checkpoint 4.3: address, guesses, topic first, fronting, question word at the end, non-human plural agreement
dialogue: A
حياك الله يا ولدي. والشقة اللي في مردف، للحين ساكن فيها؟
ḥayyāk allāh yā wildi. w ish-shigga illi fi Mirdif, lil-ḥīn sākin fīha?
Welcome, son. And the flat in Mirdif, are you still living in it?
B
الله يحييك يا عمي. هيه، للحين فيها
allāh yḥayyīk yā ʿammi. hē, lil-ḥīn fīha
Thank you, uncle. Yes, I'm still in it.
A
سمعت إن صاحب الشقة يبي يزيد الإيجار
simaʿt inn ṣāḥib ish-shigga yabi yzīd il-ījār
I heard the landlord wants to put the rent up.
B
سمعت شو يا عمي؟ منو قال لك؟
simaʿt shu yā ʿammi? minu gāl-lak?
You heard what, uncle? Who told you?
A
سيف قال لي. وانت شو بتسوي؟
Sēf gāl-li. w inta shu bitsawwi?
Sēf told me. And what are you going to do?
B
صاحب الشقة للحين ما شفناه، بس أتوقع نتفاهم
ṣāḥib ish-shigga lil-ḥīn ma shifnāh, bas atwaggaʿ nitfāham
The landlord, we haven't seen him yet, but I expect we'll come to an agreement.
A
زين، بس على هونك. الأمور هذي يبالها صبر
zēn, bas ʿala hōnak. il-umūr hādhi yabā-lha ṣabir
Good, but take it easy. Things like this need patience.
B
على عيني وراسي يا عمي
ʿala ʿēni w rāsi yā ʿammi
I'll do as you say, uncle.
items: to a woman: simaʿti shu? (سمعتي شو؟)
we haven't seen him, we didn't see him
take it easy, take your time, slowly (to a man)
to a woman: ʿala hōnich (على هونج)
it needs patience, it takes patience
with a feminine word or several things: yabā-lha ṣabir (يبالها صبر)
gladly, I'll do as you say (lit. on my eye and my head)

title: You're right, but…
goal: At a karak stand, agree with Sēf about rent and prices, fully and in part: maʿak ḥagg, ṣaḥḥ, bas…
tip: Agree fully with maʿak ḥagg 'you're right' or ana wiyyāk 'I'm with you'; add miya bil-miya for 100%. Agree in part with ṣaḥḥ, bas… 'true, but…' and add your point: ṣaḥḥ, bas mub bas il-ījār 'true, but it's not just the rent'.
grammar: recycle: comparatives and mub; agreeing fully and in part
dialogue: A
ربعي كلهم يشتكون من الإيجار هالأيام
rabʿi killhum yishtakūn min il-ījār hal-ayyām
All my mates are complaining about the rent these days.
B
معك حق، الإيجار غالي وايد
maʿak ḥagg, il-ījār ghāli wāyid
You're right, rent's really expensive.
A
هيه، والواحد شو يسوي؟ الراتب ما يزيد كل سنة
hē, w il-wāḥid shu ysawwi? ir-rātib ma yzīd kill sana
Yes, and what's a person to do? Your salary doesn't go up every year.
B
صح، بس مب بس الإيجار. الأكل بعد غالي
ṣaḥḥ, bas mub bas il-ījār. il-akil baʿad ghāli
True, but it's not just the rent. Food's expensive too.
A
بس الإيجار أكبر شي، صح ولّا لا؟
bas il-ījār akbar shay, ṣaḥḥ walla la?
But rent's the biggest thing, right or not?
B
معك حق مية بالمية. عشان جي أنا ساكن ويا ربيعي
maʿak ḥagg miya bil-miya. ʿashān chī ana sākin wiyya rbīʿi
You're a hundred percent right. That's why I live with my friend.
A
هذا غلا المعيشة اللي يتكلمون عنه في الأخبار كل يوم
hādha ghala l-maʿīsha illi yitkallmūn ʿannah fi l-akhbār kill yōm
That's the 'cost of living' they talk about on the news every day.
B
أنا وياك. بس الحمد لله، غيرنا حالهم أصعب
ana wiyyāk. bas il-ḥamdu lillāh, ghērna ḥālhum aṣʿab
I'm with you. But thank God, others have it harder.
items: to a woman: maʿich ḥagg (معج حق)
true, but…; right, but… (agreeing in part)
right or not? am I right?
I'm with you, I agree with you (to a man)
to a woman: ana wiyyāch (أنا وياج)
yishtakūn min il-ījār = they complain about the rent
others, other people (lit. other than us)
task: This week: with a tutor or exchange partner (search a tutoring site for «Emirati Arabic tutor»), ask what they think about the cost of living where they live. Agree fully with one point (maʿak ḥagg), agree in part with another (ṣaḥḥ, bas…), and give one reason of your own.

title: No, quite the opposite
goal: On the phone, disagree politely with Fahad, who thinks you should live on your own: la, bil-ʿaks; mub sharṭ; ismaḥ-li, bas…
tip: Disagree softly: la, bil-ʿaks 'no, quite the opposite'; mub lahad-daraja 'not that much'; mub sharṭ 'not necessarily'. With a friend, la tbālig! 'don't exaggerate!'. With anyone, start with ismaḥ-li, bas… 'with respect, but…'.
grammar: recycle: b-rūḥ- and comparatives; disagreeing politely
dialogue: A
هلا والله! شلونك؟
hala wallāh! shlōnak?
Hey there! How are you?
B
هلا فيك! زين الحمد لله
hala fīk! zēn il-ḥamdu lillāh
Hi! Fine, thank God.
A
سيف يقول إنك للحين ساكن ويا ربيعك. ليش ما تسكن بروحك؟
Sēf ygūl innak lil-ḥīn sākin wiyya rbīʿak. lēsh ma tiskin b-rūḥak?
Sēf says you're still living with your friend. Why don't you live on your own?
B
بروحي؟ لا، بالعكس. ويا ربيعي أحسن
b-rūḥi? la, bil-ʿaks. wiyya rbīʿi aḥsan
On my own? No, quite the opposite. It's better with my friend.
A
شلون أحسن؟ ما عندك راحة أبد!
shlōn aḥsan? ma ʿindak rāḥa abad!
How is it better? You get no peace at all!
B
لا تبالغ، مب لهالدرجة. ربيعي هادي، وأغلب الوقت في الدوام
la tbālig, mub lahad-daraja. rbīʿi hādi, w aghlab il-wagt fi d-dawām
Don't exaggerate, it's not that bad. My friend's quiet, and he's at work most of the time.
A
إيه، بس صدقني، الشقة بروحك أحسن لك
ēh, bas ṣaddigni, ish-shigga b-rūḥak aḥsan lak
Yeah, but believe me, a flat of your own is better for you.
B
اسمح لي، بس مب شرط. بروحي بدفع الإيجار كله!
ismaḥ-li, bas mub sharṭ. b-rūḥi badfaʿ il-ījār killah!
With respect, not necessarily. On my own I'd pay the whole rent!
A
زين زين، خلاص. كل واحد له رأيه، وانت أدرى بحالك
zēn zēn, khalāṣ. kill wāḥid lah raʼyah, w inta adra b-ḥālak
OK, OK, fine. Everyone's entitled to their opinion, and you know your own situation best.
items: no, quite the opposite; not at all
not that much, it's not that bad (lit. not to that degree)
to a woman: la tbālgīn (لا تبالغين); friends only
with respect, but…; excuse me, but… (to a man)
everyone's entitled to their opinion (lit. everyone has his opinion)
you know your own situation best (to a man)
(recognise); to a woman: inti adra b-ḥālich (انتي أدرى بحالج)

title: Honestly, I hadn't thought of it like that
goal: At the office, with the team around, Maryam says living near work would save you time; concede her point but keep one of your own
tip: Concede in two steps: first give way, wallāh ma fakkart fīha chī 'honestly, I hadn't thought of it like that', then maʿich ḥagg (to a woman). Keep your own point with bas: mub il-ḥīn, bas ʿajbatni l-fikra 'not now, but I like the idea'.
grammar: recycle: lō + present, il-muhimm; conceding a point
dialogue: A
انت كل يوم تسوق من مردف؟ ما تتعب؟
inta kill yōm tsūg min Mirdif? ma titʿab?
You drive from Mirdif every day? Don't you get tired?
B
لا، عادي. مردف مب بعيد
la, ʿādi. Mirdif mub baʿīd
No, it's fine. Mirdif's not far.
A
بس لو تسكن قريب من الدوام، توفر وقت وبترول
bas lō tiskin garīb min id-dawām, twaffir wagt w batrōl
But if you lived near work, you'd save time and petrol.
B
يمكن، بس الإيجار هني أغلى
yimkin, bas il-ījār hni aghla
Maybe, but the rent here is higher.
A
صح، بس فكر في الزحمة كل يوم، الصبح والعصر
ṣaḥḥ, bas fakkir fi z-zaḥma kill yōm, iṣ-ṣubḥ w il-ʿaṣir
True, but think about the traffic every day, morning and afternoon.
B
والله ما فكرت فيها جي. معج حق
wallāh ma fakkart fīha chī. maʿich ḥagg
Honestly, I hadn't thought of it like that. You're right.
A
يعني بتنتقل؟ الشباب يقولون المسافة تفرق وايد على الأعصاب
yaʿni bitintigil? ish-shabāb ygūlūn il-masāfa tfarrig wāyid ʿala l-aʿṣāb
So you'll move? The guys say the distance makes a big difference to your nerves.
B
مب الحين، بس عجبتني الفكرة
mub il-ḥīn, bas ʿajbatni l-fikra
Not now, but I like the idea.
A
على راحتك. المهم تكون مرتاح
ʿala rāḥtak. il-muhimm tkūn mirtāḥ
Up to you. What matters is that you're comfortable.
B
صدقتي، المهم الراحة
ṣidagti, il-muhimm ir-rāḥa
You're right, comfort's what matters.
items: I hadn't thought of it like that
you save time (to a man); it (f.) saves time
to a woman: twaffrīn wagt (توفرين وقت)
don't you get tired? (to a man)
to a woman: ma titʿabīn? (ما تتعبين؟)
on your nerves, for your nerves
what matters is that you're comfortable (to a man)
to a woman: il-muhimm tkūnīn mirtāḥa (المهم تكونين مرتاحة)

title: The good thing about it, and the problem
goal: Weigh up the pros and cons of a cheaper flat with Sēf: il-ḥilu fīha…, bas il-mushkila…, min ṣōb thāni…
tip: List the good side with il-ḥilu fīha 'the good thing about it' and the bad with bas il-mushkila 'but the problem is' or ʿēbha 'its drawback'. Balance them with min ṣōb… w min ṣōb thāni 'on one hand… on the other', and hedge with ʿala ḥasab 'it depends'.
grammar: recycle: comparatives (arkhaṣ, awsaʿ) and inn; weighing pros and cons
dialogue: A
شفت الإعلان اللي طرشته؟ الشقة هذي إيجارها أرخص من شقتكم
shift il-iʿlān illi ṭarrashtah? ish-shigga hādhi ījārha arkhaṣ min shiggatkum
Did you see the ad I sent? This flat's rent is cheaper than your flat's.
B
شفته. الحلو فيها إنها أرخص وأوسع
shiftah. il-ḥilu fīha innha arkhaṣ w awsaʿ
I saw it. The good thing about it is it's cheaper and bigger.
A
وفيها مسبح بعد، تحت في العمارة
w fīha masbaḥ baʿad, taḥt fi l-ʿimāra
And it's got a pool too, downstairs in the building.
B
صح، بس المشكلة إنها بعيدة عن الجامعة
ṣaḥḥ, bas il-mushkila innha baʿīda ʿan il-jāmʿa
True, but the problem is it's far from the university.
A
يعني من صوب أرخص، ومن صوب ثاني بعيدة
yaʿni min ṣōb arkhaṣ, w min ṣōb thāni baʿīda
So on one hand it's cheaper, and on the other it's far.
B
بالضبط. وعيبها بعد إن ما في مترو قريب
biẓ-ẓabṭ. w ʿēbha baʿad inn ma fī mitrō garīb
Exactly. And another drawback is there's no metro nearby.
A
يعني كل شقة فيها شي حلو وفيها عيوب، ما في شي كامل
yaʿni kill shigga fīha shay ḥilu w fīha ʿuyūb, ma fī shay kāmil
So every flat has something good and some drawbacks; nothing's perfect.
B
على حسب الإيجار اللي بيطلبه صاحب الشقة
ʿala ḥasab il-ījār illi biyiṭlubah ṣāḥib ish-shigga
It depends on the rent the landlord's going to ask for.
A
صح. كلمه أول، وبعدين شوف
ṣaḥḥ. kallmah awwal, w baʿdēn shūf
Right. Talk to him first, and then see.
items: about a masculine thing: il-ḥilu fīh (الحلو فيه)
bas il-mushkila inn… = but the problem is that…
on the other hand (lit. from another side)
Kuwait: min nāḥya thānya (من ناحية ثانية)
its (f.) drawback, the downside of it
about a masculine thing: ʿēbah (عيبه); ʿēb on its own means 'rude'

title: With respect, uncle, the difference is big
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Sēf there, disagree with him respectfully about moving further out, then give way on one point
tip: With an elder, agree first and only then say bas: ṣaḥḥ kalāmak yā ʿammi, bas il-farg kbīr 'you're right, uncle, but the difference is big'. Give way with ṣaḥḥ, mub qalīla 'true, that's not nothing', and close with yimkin ma yistāhil 'maybe it's not worth it'.
grammar: recycle: comparatives (aghla min) and cham; disagreeing with an elder, conceding
dialogue: A
سمعت إنك تفكر تغير شقتك. صج؟
simaʿt innak tfakkir tghayyir shiggtak. ṣij?
I heard you're thinking of changing flats. Is that true?
B
يمكن يا عمي. في شقة بعيدة شوي، بس إيجارها أرخص
yimkin yā ʿammi. fī shigga baʿīda shwayy, bas ījārha arkhaṣ
Maybe, uncle. There's a flat a bit further out, but its rent is cheaper.
A
يا ولدي، أنا دوم أقول لعيالي: الوقت من ذهب
yā wildi, ana dōm agūl ḥagg ʿyāli: il-wagt min dhahab
Son, I always tell my children: time is gold.
B
صح كلامك يا عمي، بس الفرق كبير
ṣaḥḥ kalāmak yā ʿammi, bas il-farg kbīr
You're right, uncle, but the difference is big.
A
زين، وكم ساعة بتضيع كل يوم في الطريق؟
zēn, w cham sāʿa bitẓīʿ kill yōm fi ṭ-ṭarīg?
All right, and how many hours will you lose every day on the road?
B
ساعة تقريبا… صح، مب قليلة
sāʿa tagrīban… ṣaḥḥ, mub qalīla
About an hour… True, that's not nothing.
A
احسبها زين: يستاهل ولّا ما يستاهل؟
iḥsibha zēn: yistāhil walla ma yistāhil?
Work it out properly: is it worth it or not?
B
والله يا عمي، يمكن ما يستاهل. بفكر فيها زين
wallāh yā ʿammi, yimkin ma yistāhil. bafakkir fīha zēn
Honestly, uncle, maybe it isn't worth it. I'll think it over properly.
A
الله يوفقك يا ولدي
allāh ywaffgak yā wildi
God help you get it right, son.
B
آمين يا عمي
āmīn yā ʿammi
Amen, uncle.
items: the difference is big, it's a big difference
time is gold, time is precious (a saying)
(it, f.) will be lost, will go to waste
that's not nothing, that's quite a lot (f.)
with a masculine word: mub qalīl (مب قليل)
work it out, do the sums (to a man)
you're thinking of changing (to a man)
to a woman: tfakkrīn tghayyrīn (تفكرين تغيرين)
culture: Friendly words don't travel upwards. Yā rayyāl is fine with Sēf but a real faux pas with an elder or in a meeting; to someone like Bū Rāshid it's yā ʿammi, and ṭawīl il-ʿumr is used respectfully to elders, sheikhs and strangers. In this scene B also agrees first, ṣaḥḥ kalāmak yā ʿammi, before his 'but'.

title: Bottom line: we're staying
goal: On a call, tell Sēf how the talk with the landlord went, weigh it up and say what you've decided
tip: Sum up and decide: garār ḥilu 'a good decision', ḥasabt-ha 'I worked it out', garrarna 'we've decided'. You'll also hear il-khulāṣa 'in short, the bottom line'. Recycle the question word at the end: w huwa gāl shu?
grammar: recycle: question word at the end, comparatives; summing up and deciding
dialogue: A
ها؟ شو صار ويا صاحب الشقة؟
hā? shu ṣār wiyya ṣāḥib ish-shigga?
So? What happened with the landlord?
B
يبي يزيد الإيجار شوي
yabi yzīd il-ījār shwayy
He wants to put the rent up a bit.
A
وانت شو قلت له؟ وافقت على طول؟
w inta shu gilt-lah? wāfagt ʿala ṭūl?
And what did you tell him? Did you agree straight away?
B
لا، قلت له الزيادة وايد علينا
la, gilt-lah iz-ziyāda wāyid ʿalēna
No, I told him the increase is too much for us.
A
وهو قال شو؟
w huwa gāl shu?
And he said what?
B
بالأخير تفاهمنا على نص اللي طلبه
bil-akhīr tfāhamna ʿala nuṣṣ illi ṭalabah
In the end we agreed on half of what he asked for.
A
ما شاء الله عليك! يعني بتقعدون في مردف؟
mā shāʼ allāh ʿalēk! yaʿni bitigʿdūn fi Mirdif?
Well done you! So you're staying in Mirdif?
B
هيه. حسبتها: الشقة البعيدة أرخص، بس ما تستاهل
hē. ḥasabt-ha: ish-shigga l-baʿīda arkhaṣ, bas ma tistāhil
Yes. I worked it out: the far flat is cheaper, but it isn't worth it.
A
على كل حال، قرار حلو. والخلاصة، انت ومردف ما تفترقون!
ʿala kill ḥāl, garār ḥilu. w il-khulāṣa, inta w Mirdif ma tiftargūn!
Anyway, good decision. Bottom line: you and Mirdif are inseparable!
B
بالضبط! خلاص، قررنا: قاعدين
biẓ-ẓabṭ! khalāṣ, garrarna: gāʿdīn
Exactly! That's it, we've decided: we're staying.
items: you agreed straight away (to a man); I agreed straight away
to a woman: wāfagti ʿala ṭūl (وافقتي على طول)
the increase, the rise (in rent or prices)
too much for me: wāyid ʿalay (وايد علي)
half of what he asked for
are you staying? will you stay? (to a group, or about you and others)
to one man: bitigʿid; to a woman: bitigʿdīn (بتقعدين)
I worked it out, I did the sums; you worked it out (to a man)
task: This week: in Talk, ask your partner to play your landlord, who wants to put the rent up. Disagree politely (ismaḥ-li, bas…; mub sharṭ), give way on one point (maʿak ḥagg, bas…) and finish with an agreement (tfāhamna ʿala…). Keep it going for 8 turns, and don't invent any official rules: just talk it through.
